title: Advanced comparison
tagline: Fine degrees of comparison: nowhere near, every bit as, by far, and like vs as.
exam: Reading & Use of English Part 4 — key word transformations (NOWHERE, FAR, BIT, MUCH, HAD, IF)
Reading & Use of English Part 2 — open cloze (as, than, like)
Writing Part 2 — reviews and reports: precise, graded comparisons
Speaking Part 2 — comparing photographs with more than a flat comparative
why: At C1, a flat comparative such as 'more interesting' or 'as good as' reads as B2. Examiners expect graded, precise comparison: how far below, how exactly equal, or how much further ahead something is. Use of English Part 4 regularly sets these expressions as key words, and Part 2's open cloze often tests the one small word — as, than, like — that a weaker answer gets wrong.

diagrams.title: like vs as vs as if

rows.label: Function
cells: a real role, job or true manner

rows.label: Followed by
cells: a clause, often past for the unreal

rows.label: Example
cells: Like her sister, Nadia plays the violin.
She works as a tour guide in Cusco.
He talks as if he owned the place.

rows.label: Common error
cells: She works like a guide (but she IS one)
as if he owns it (too literal for a firm unreal impression)

diagrams.title: The more..., the more... (with ellipsis)
diagrams.caption: In speech and informal writing, the second clause is often left out entirely: 'The sooner, the better.'

head: Pattern
Structure
Example
rows: the + comparative, the + comparative
The + comp + clause, the + comp + clause
The earlier we leave, the more time we'll have at the ruins.
nowhere near / nothing like
nowhere near / nothing like + as...as
This year's team is nowhere near as strong as last year's.
by far
by far + the + superlative
Cusco is by far the most visited city on the tour.
every bit as / just as
every bit as / just as + adjective + as
Nadia is every bit as capable as the head girl.
not so much X as Y
not so much + noun/clause + as + noun/clause
It's not so much a rule as a strong recommendation.
comparative + than + clause
comparative + than + had been expected/anticipated
The exam was harder than we had expected.
as...as any
as + adjective + as any + noun
She's as dedicated as any student I've taught.
all the more
all the more + adjective (+ because/since)
The win was all the more satisfying because no one expected it.

use.point: Emphasising how far apart two things are

examples.text: The new stadium is nowhere near as big as the one in Lima.
examples.note: nowhere near + as...as, a strong negative comparison

examples.text: This translation is nothing like as accurate as the original.
examples.note: nothing like, interchangeable with nowhere near, slightly more informal

examples.text: Of all the entries, Sofia's essay was by far the most original.

use.point: Emphasising how close two things are

examples.text: Liam is every bit as competitive as his older brother.
examples.note: every bit as = fully as, emphatic equality

examples.text: The coastal route is just as scenic as the mountain one, and far safer.
examples.note: just as, slightly less emphatic than every bit as

examples.text: She argues as convincingly as any lawyer I've watched.
examples.note: as + adjective + as any + noun, a strong claim among the best examples

use.point: Making a fine distinction, not a simple comparison

examples.text: It was not so much a mistake as a missed opportunity.
examples.note: correcting how something should be understood, not its size

examples.text: The result was all the more impressive given how little time they had.
examples.note: all the more + adjective, often followed by a reason

examples.text: Winning felt all the more satisfying because nobody had expected it.
examples.note: all the more before an adjective, with because/since/given

use.point: Comparatives with a following clause, and like vs as vs as if

examples.text: The turnout was far higher than the organisers had anticipated.
examples.note: comparative + than + clause, often past perfect for an earlier expectation

examples.text: Like her mother, Nadia has a talent for languages.
He spoke as if the decision had already been made.
examples.note: as if + past (hypothetical), even about the present

watch_out.wrong: This year's team is nowhere near strong as last year's.
watch_out.right: This year's team is nowhere near as strong as last year's.
watch_out.why: nowhere near needs as before the adjective: nowhere near as + adjective + as.

watch_out.wrong: She is just so talented as her sister.
watch_out.right: She is just as talented as her sister.
watch_out.why: just as, not just so, before the adjective in this comparative pattern.

watch_out.wrong: It's not so much a rule than a recommendation.
watch_out.right: It's not so much a rule as a recommendation.
watch_out.why: not so much X pairs with as, never than.

watch_out.wrong: The exam was harder that we had expected.
watch_out.right: The exam was harder than we had expected.
watch_out.why: a comparative clause is introduced by than, not that.

watch_out.wrong: He talked as he owned the place.
watch_out.right: He talked as if he owned the place.
watch_out.why: an unreal impression needs as if / as though, not as alone.

watch_out.wrong: She works like a tour guide, taking groups out every weekend.
watch_out.right: She works as a tour guide, taking groups out every weekend.
watch_out.why: as + role/job describes what someone genuinely is; like compares to something they are not.

dialogue.title: Comparing notes after the debate
dialogue.context: Miss Vega asks the team how the inter-school debate against San Martín went, and they compare this year's performance with last year's.

lines.speaker: Miss Vega
lines.text: So, how did the debate team do against San Martín?

lines.speaker: Liam
lines.text: Honestly? We were nowhere near as prepared as they were.

lines.speaker: Sofia
lines.text: Speak for yourself — Nadia was every bit as sharp as their top speaker.

lines.speaker: Nadia
lines.text: Thanks, but their rebuttals were by far the strongest part of their case.

lines.speaker: Mateo
lines.text: It wasn't so much the arguments as the timing that let us down.

lines.speaker: Miss Vega
lines.text: Fair point. Was it harder than you expected?

lines.speaker: Liam
lines.text: Much harder than we had prepared for, yes.

lines.speaker: Sofia
lines.text: He spoke as if he'd done this a hundred times before.

lines.speaker: Nadia
lines.text: Losing was all the more frustrating because we'd won last year.

lines.speaker: Mateo
lines.text: Still, Sofia argued as confidently as any senior on that stage.

lines.speaker: Miss Vega
lines.text: Good. Then next term we train like a team that expects to win.

items.sentence: Our results were ___ as impressive as we'd hoped.
items.why: nowhere near + as...as shows a big gap below the standard hoped for.

items.sentence: Of all the entries, this one was ___ the most original.
items.why: by far intensifies a superlative — the most original.

items.sentence: She's ___ dedicated as any athlete I've coached.
items.why: as + adjective + as any + noun claims equality with the very best examples.

items.sentence: It isn't ___ a punishment as a chance to reflect.
items.why: not so much X as Y reframes how something should be understood, not how big it is.

items.sentence: The film was funnier ___ the critics had suggested.
items.why: a comparative clause is introduced by than, not that.

items.sentence: He walked in ___ he'd never left.
items.why: as if + clause gives an unreal impression; like needs a noun, not a clause, here.

items.sentence: Nadia trains ___ a professional, six days a week.
items.why: as + role describes what someone genuinely is; like would suggest she isn't really a professional.

practice.instructions: Complete each sentence with one or two words so that it is grammatically correct.

items.sentence: This laptop is nowhere ___ as fast as the one at school.
Of the whole squad, Mateo trains ___ far the hardest.
Nadia is every ___ as capable as the head girl.
It's not so much a rule ___ a strong recommendation.
The turnout was higher ___ the organisers had expected.
He spoke as ___ the decision had already been made.
The win felt all the ___ satisfying because nobody expected it.

practice.instructions: Complete the second sentence so that it has a similar meaning to the first, using the word given. Do not change the word given. Use between two and five words.

items.first: Our team wasn't nearly as prepared as theirs.
This entry was clearly the most original of them all.
items.second_end: the most original of them all.

items.first: Liam is fully as competitive as his older brother.
items.second_end: as competitive as his older brother.

items.first: This was more a missed opportunity than a genuine mistake.
items.second_end: a mistake as a missed opportunity.

items.first: The exam was harder than we expected.
From the way he spoke, it seemed the decision had already been made.
items.second_end: the decision had already been made.

summary: Use nowhere near / nothing like for a big gap below, and every bit as / just as for genuine equality.
By far intensifies a superlative; all the more intensifies an adjective, often with a reason attached.
Not so much X as Y corrects how something should be understood, not how big it is.
A comparative clause takes than, not that: harder than we had expected.
Like takes a noun; as names a real role; as if / as though gives an impression, often unreal.
